hero.title: Read It Your Way
hero.subtitle: More than a reading app, a new home for all your ebooks, audiobooks, comics and manga.

customize.title: Your Books, Your Rules
body: With Thorium Reader, you can switch between reading or listening whenever you want… or even do both at the same time.
Take full control of your reading experience with easy to use, yet powerful, user settings.

library.title: Bring Your Own Books
body: We built a place where all books are welcome.
Download on the Web, borrow from a library, buy from a bookstore… but read them all in Thorium Reader.

section.title: Join the Adventure!
subtitle: Thorium Reader is completely free and maintained by a non-profit organization.
Available on iOS, iPadOS, Windows, macOS and Linux.

ios.title: iOS and iPadOS
ios.body: Thorium Reader is available on the App Store for iOS, iPadOS and macOS devices running on Apple Silicon.

desktop.title: Windows, macOS, Linux
body: If you're on Windows, we recommend getting Thorium Reader from the Microsoft Store.
Direct downloads are also available for Windows, macOS and Linux.

steps: Download the {{ windowsExe }} file to your Windows device.
Open the Explorer and navigate to folder where you downloaded the file.
Double-click the downloaded *.exe file. Double-click the downloaded installer file and complete the installation process. Managed devices may require admin authorization to install.
If you're using a Windows device running on ARM, make sure that you use the {{ windowsArm }}.
Download the {{ macosArm }} file to your macOS device.
Open the Finder and navigate to Downloads.
Now drag and drop the application icon to the Applications folder to install the application.
Close the window and press the eject button in Finder to dismount the image.
If you're using a macOS device running on an Intel processor, make sure that you use the {{ macosX64 }}.
Download either the {{ linuxAppImage }} or {{ linuxDeb }} to your Linux device.
If you're running Linux on an ARM device, make sure to use alternate download links for the {{ linuxAppImageArm }} or {{ linuxDebArm }}.

items.question: Is Thorium Reader free?
answer: Yes, Thorium Reader is free on all platforms.
It's developed by EDRLab (European Digital Reading Lab), a non-profit association dedicated to open standards, literacy and accessibility.
With Thorium Reader, we contribute directly to the development of Readium toolkits, used by hundreds of reading applications.

items.question: What devices are compatible with Thorium Reader?
answer: If you own an iPhone or an iPad, Thorium Reader can run on any device running at least iOS/iPadOS 26
On Windows, it requires Windows 10 and up
On macOS, it requires macOS 12 Monterey and up

items.question: Which file formats are compatible with Thorium Reader?
Can I open DRM protected files with Thorium Reader?
answer: Yes, as long as they use Readium LCP, an interoperable ISO standard for DRM.
Readium LCP protected files use a license file (with an .lcpl file extension) that's compatible with EPUB, PDF or Readium Audiobooks.

items.question: Can I use Thorium Reader offline?
answer: Yes, as long as you're reading or listening to publications that you've downloaded rather than streamed.
To read LCP protected files, Thorium Reader needs an online access at least once, but it doesn't require a connection after that.

items.question: Can I buy ebooks, audiobooks, comics or manga from a retailer?
answer: Yes, Thorium Reader is compatible with any retailer that sells Readium LCP protected or DRM free publications.
Check our support page to explore a list of retailers that you can buy content from and read in Thorium Reader.

items.question: Can I borrow ebooks, audiobooks, comics, manga, newspapers or magazines from a library?
answer: Yes, as long as your library uses Readium LCP to protects these downloads using a format compatible with Thorium Reader.
In the future, we'll also embed a list of libraries directly in our app, making it easier to browse, search, place a hold and borrow.

items.question: Can I download free content with Thorium Reader?
answer: Yes, Thorium Reader is fully compatible with Project Gutenberg, Librivox and many other sources that you can download public domain or open licensed content from.
In the future, we'll also embed a number of them directly in our app, to make it easier to download free ebooks and audiobooks.
